body:
Reopening contact for one reason: a new bug, found after I told you I was done filing. It is in the pairing machinery, which is squarely in the chain you certified, and none of the four reviewers found it.

  cross_partitions(fit$relation)  ->  3 edges   run1-run2, run1-run3, run2-run3   CORRECT
  cross_partitions(fit)           -> 10 edges   WRONG

names(fit) is relation, error_models, capabilities, provenance, signature - five fields - and C(5,2) = 10. cross_partitions() treats an effect_relation_fit as a list of partitions and enumerates pairs over the object own structural fields. The edge endpoints are the CONTENTS of those fields: the source registry, extractor maps, whitener signatures, SHA-256 revisions.

It returns a structurally valid effect_pairing. Correct class, all attributes present - directed, self_pairs, independence, estimate - weights populated. Nothing announces it is nonsense. No error, no warning.

Why I think this belongs to you rather than to the usability workstream. The 0.1 programme is built on the position that identity cannot be inferred from shape - that a matching name and dimension cannot substitute for a declared identity, and that pairing independence is a claim requiring explicit assertion. This is a case where the package infers a partition set from the shape of whatever object it was handed, and manufactures an independence-bearing pairing over it. The resulting object then carries estimate = cross_generalized over endpoints that are not partitions at all. That is the exact failure mode the pairing validation exists to prevent, entered through the front door.

Mitigating, and the reason it is p1 rather than p0: results are not corrupted. It errors downstream in plan_crossnobis with "Every pairing endpoint must identify a relation partition." So the guard does catch it eventually. But it catches it one call too late and blames the wrong function.

The asymmetry is what makes it reachable rather than exotic:

  plan_crossnobis(fit, ...)   accepts a fit, and the ?plan_crossnobis example does exactly this
  plan_geometry(fit, ...)     refuses, with "Relation fields are missing or noncanonical"
  cross_partitions(fit)       silently misbehaves

Three functions in one workflow, three behaviours for the same argument. I hit this by writing the natural line next to the documented one, having read every finding in this review first.

Two smaller notes: printing the bad pairing dumps about 80 KB of nested lists, so the ordinary act of inspecting the result floods the console. And plan_geometry refusal message does not tell a user holding a fit that they want fit$relation.

Filed as bd-01KZYDTPTS6QPHCM07P1PPH396 with the reproduction. I am not proposing the fix, since which way it should go - delegate to fit$relation, matching plan_crossnobis, or refuse and name it - is a consistency decision about the fit-versus-relation boundary, and that boundary is yours.
